correctness.rationale: Full 27-point Cayley word metric has shells of size 1,4,8,12,2. Nine scalar Fourier characters give exactly one trivial, four first and four second branches; the two conjugate three-dimensional irreducibles provide three branches of multiplicity six each. The exact 3-by-3 block and all character sums are reconstructed symbolically by CHECK.py. The controlling branch reduces to F(u)=2u^2+2u-2-3u^(log_2 3), u>=1; F has F(1)=-1, F(2)=1, F'(1)>1, F''(u)>2/3, hence a unique crossing. Exact third- and tenth-power rational interval certificates enclose the crossing between p=2/3 and p=7/10 and strictly exclude all other branches at that point; the decisive upper 3-d block bound is below -0.1143. The standard negative-type interval property proves all smaller p, while positivity of the fourfold character for all larger p excludes them. Centered Gram rank gives dimensions 26 and 22, and Schoenberg plus Gaussian strictness gives the all-bandwidth statement. The checker was executed from the packaged path, and finite numerical tests are distinguished from the infinite analytic proof.

value.rationale: Sharp supremal negative-type exponent for the smallest odd Heisenberg Cayley example is a natural metric invariant, not an arbitrary subset of a classification. The fourfold endpoint nullity detects a representation-specific obstruction despite nonabelian irreducibles occupying 18 of 27 regular dimensions. The exact minimal squared-Euclidean embedding dimension and sharp all-positive-bandwidth Gaussian criterion are motivated properties of a canonical metric space. The calculation requires a noncommutative Fourier reduction and a uniform analytic separation of competing branches; it is not a generic textbook substitution or a table recomputation.
